newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier '96 watercraft sales up 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier '96 watercraft sales up 20 pct.

text.p: Canadian transportation giant Bombardier Inc said on Thursday that sales of its personal watercraft and jet boat products showed solid growth in 1996, with substantial increases in market share worldwide.
Dealer bookings for 1997 promise continued strength for the company's marine product lines, Bombardier said.

"We're concluding a robust season reflecting a 20 percent increase in retail sales of SEA-DOO watercraft over the previous year," Pierre Beaudoin, president and chief operating officer of Bombardier's motorized consumer products group, said in a statement.
Retail sales of the group's jet boat line increased 35 percent, Bombardier said.
Sales increased despite unseasonably wet or cool weather this past summer which curtailed the season in some areas of North America, the company said.
The SEA-DOO watercraft line increased its North American market share to 50.8 percent at the end of August, up from a 42 percent share in the previous year.
"We experienced significant growth in the three-seater category, up 50 percent in units sold at retail over 1995, and we consider that a strong bellwether," Beaudoin said.
Bombardier said demand is strong for these multi-passenger watercraft among first-time buyers.

The company's stock has suffered recently due to market concerns that the popularity of the jet ski is fading, analysts said. But Beaudoin said industry research shows that personal watercraft continue to draw significant numbers of new buyers. "Six out of ten owners surveyed at year-end 1995 were first-time buyers," he said, adding that the company's research shows that trend continuing.
Bombardier's class B stock ended up 0.10 at 17.90 after losing 0.95 over the past two sessions.
